title: Sunny and the Bush Silence | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka walks deeper and deeper into the bush until she finds the quietest place she has ever been — where even her own breathing feels like the loudest thing in the world. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
Sunny walked toward the quiet.

Not away from noise — the bush was never exactly noisy at night. But there were layers. Near the creek there were water sounds. Near the clearing there were crickets. Near the old gum trees there were always small rustlings.

She walked past all of them, deeper into the bush, following a thread of stillness that seemed to pull her gently forward.

And then she was there.

She didn't know how she knew, but she knew. This small place — surrounded on all sides by dense understorey, the ground soft with fallen leaves — was the quietest place in the whole bush.

She stopped.

The silence pressed in gently from all sides.

She could hear her own breathing. In and out. The small sound of her feet shifting on the leaves. A single distant cricket, so far away it was almost imaginary.

That was all.

She had never heard so little in all her life, and it was the most beautiful thing she had ever heard.

She sat down very slowly, trying not to disturb the quiet.

The silence received her.

She sat in it for a long time, breathing slowly, feeling the quiet settle into every part of her — into her paws, her chest, behind her eyes.

Full of nothing. Full of everything.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, bush silence. Goodnight, little one.
